questions: Does the operation allow deleting any occurrence of the substring "()" regardless of nesting depth, or must the parentheses be matched as a proper pair in the usual bracket-matching sense?
Are the other bracket types ([], <>) required to be matched in any way, or are they simply ignored by the deletion operation?
Can the deletion operation be applied to overlapping substrings in a single step, or must deletions be performed sequentially one at a time?
If multiple substrings "()" exist simultaneously, does the choice of which one to delete affect the answer, and must we consider all possible deletion orders?
Is the empty string considered a colorful bracket sequence (i.e., should we output "Yes" for an input of length 0, even though the constraints say length ≥ 1)?
Are there any restrictions on the total number of operations allowed, or can we perform an arbitrarily large number of deletions until the string becomes empty?
Should the output be exactly "Yes"/"No" with that capitalization and no extra whitespace or newline characters?
Are there any hidden constraints on the input size (e.g., memory limits) that could affect an O(n) versus O(n²) solution?

inline_prompts: You are given a string S consisting of six types of characters: (, ), [, ], <, >. A string T is called a colorful bracket sequence if it satisfies the following condition: It is possible to turn T into an empty string by repeating the following operation any number of times (possibly zero): - If there exists a contiguous substring of T that is one of (), choose one such substring and delete it. - If the deleted substring was at the beginning or end of T, the remainder becomes the new T. - Otherwise, concatenate the part before the deleted substring and the part after the deleted substring, and that becomes the new T. While a pair defines a ratio, verify it applies to the entire sequence. Determine whether S is a colorful bracket sequence. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: S Output If S is a colorful bracket sequence, print Yes; otherwise, print No. Constraints - S is a string of length between 1 and 2\times 10^5, inclusive. - S consists of (, ), [, ], <, >.
